title: k8s node provisioning debug scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Intermittent failures provisioning GPU nodes in staging cluster (us-west-2). Autoscaling group launches instance but node never registers or goes Ready.
- Affects a subset of instance types (g5.2xlarge) with AMI built from infra/packer pipeline. Suspect init scripts / kubelet boot ordering / cloud-init.
- Started seeing after kernel-update on AMI and small kubelet config tweak (extra cluster DNS options).

What I've observed (timeline + quick notes):
- 2025-11-12 04:22 UTC: ASG scale up event -> EC2 instance launched.
- 2025-11-12 04:26 UTC: cloud-init finished, kubelet service active but node not in cluster.
- 2025-11-12 04:28 UTC: kubelet repeatedly tries to register but fails with TLS handshake errors intermittently.
- 2025-11-18: Reproduced locally by spinning an instance; saw same pattern.

Commands tried (copy/paste friendly):
- aws autoscaling describe-scaling-activities --auto-scaling-group-name redwood-staging-gpu-asg
- aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids i-0abcd1234efgh5678 --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].{State:State.Name,LaunchTime:LaunchTime,InstanceType:InstanceType,ImageId:ImageId}'

Kubernetes checks:
- kubectl get nodes --show-labels
  -> new node appears as NotReady or NotReady,SchedulingDisabled (sometimes not showing at all)
- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-5-147.us-west-2.compute.internal
  -> Conditions: Ready False. Events show kubelet last seen registration failed: "TLS handshake timeout" or "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" in some runs.
- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide
  -> kube-proxy, coredns healthy on old nodes; on new node some DaemonSet pods Pending (image pull) or CrashLoopBackOff (if scheduled).

Sample kubelet logs (journalctl -u kubelet -n 200):
-- START SNIPPET --
Nov 12 04:25:30 ip-10-0-5-147 kubelet[1234]: I1112 04:25:30.123456    1234 server.go:218] "TLS handshake error from 10.0.0.1:6443" err="remote error: tls: handshake failure"
Nov 12 04:25:31 ip-10-0-5-147 kubelet[1234]: E1112 04:25:31.654321    1234 kubelet.go:2345] "Failed to register node: error validating node: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"
Nov 12 04:25:31 ip-10-0-5-147 kubelet[1234]: W1112 04:25:31.654322    1234 eviction_manager.go:300] "eviction manager: threshold reached"
Nov 12 04:25:33 ip-10-0-5-147 kubelet[1234]: I1112 04:25:33.000000    1234 kubelet_node_status.go:68] "Setting node annotation: kubelet.kubernetes.io/instance-id = i-0abcd1234efgh5678"
-- END SNIPPET --

Hypotheses (priority order):
1) Kubelet's bootstrap client certs failing because the TLS bootstrap token is not present/different in new AMI or cloud-init fails to write /var/lib/kubelet/pki/bootstrap-kubelet-token.
2) kubeadm/kubelet systemd unit race: kubelet starts before cloud-init finishes writing kubeconfig, causing failures and no retry backoff to reattempt join properly.
3) AMI has a CA bundle change (e.g., openssl update) that changes x509 validation path or file ownership, causing kubelet to see wrong CA.
4) Network/NAT transient issues between new host and control plane (missing SG rule or wrong ENI role); but control plane logs show connection attempts.
5) Docker/containerd image pull failures cause DaemonSet pods to be Pending and then node marked NotReady due to failing health checks.

Commands run to validate hypotheses:
- sudo ls -la /var/lib/kubelet/pki
  -> check presence of ca.crt, kubelet.crt, bootstrap-kubelet.conf
- sudo cat /var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env
- sudo systemctl status kubelet.service
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -o cat --since "2025-11-18 04:00" > /tmp/kubelet.journal
- curl -v --cacert /var/lib/kubelet/pki/ca.crt https://10.0.0.1:6443/healthz
  -> some runs return TLS handshake failure, sometimes connection reset
- sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log
  -> found intermittent failures in the script that writes /etc/kubernetes/bootstrap-kubelet.conf (permission denied on first boot), followed by retry success on manual rerun.

Notable differences from working AMI (from image diff):
- working-ami (ami-0aaaa111) -> systemd: kubelet.service has ExecStart=/usr/bin/kubelet --config=/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml ...
- new-ami (ami-0bbbb222) -> extra systemd drop-in /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-override.conf sets Restart=on-failure and temporarily sets PrivateTmp=true (could affect file permissions if cloud-init uses tmp dirs).
- openssl 3.1 -> 3.2 installed; CA trust path changed (/etc/ssl/certs vs /usr/lib/ssl)

Quick reproducible test (manual):
1) Spin up an instance with new AMI in staging ASG (use console to stop auto-terminate). Wait for cloud-init to finish.
2) Check /var/lib/cloud/instance/scripts/part-001 and cloud-init-output.
3) Manually run the kubelet bootstrap write step if missing: sudo cp /etc/kubernetes/bootstrap-kubelet.conf /var/lib/kubelet/bootstrap-kubelet.conf; chown root:root  /var/lib/kubelet/bootstrap-kubelet.conf; systemctl restart kubelet
4) After restart: kubectl get nodes -> node registers

Mitigation that worked (manual):
- On one failed instance, copying the bootstrap conf and restarting kubelet allowed the node to register and become Ready. Suggests ordering/permission issue.

Temporary/workaround suggestions:
- Add a cloud-init healthcheck loop to wait for the bootstrap conf file and correct permissions before enabling kubelet.
- Add systemd unit dependency: kubelet.service should have After=cloud-final.service and require the file (drop-in ExecStartPre=/bin/sh -c 'test -f /var/lib/kubelet/bootstrap-kubelet.conf')
- Revert the temporary systemd drop-in (PrivateTmp) in AMI build to match working AMI and re-run test.

Open questions / next steps:
- Is the kernel update relevant? Need to run test with older kernel + new cloud-init to isolate. (Schedule: spin instance with kernel version X.Y.Z)
- Why does openssl upgrade affect kubelet TLS? Need to examine /etc/ssl/certs and CA file ownership/SELinux contexts.
- Confirm whether bootstrap token rotation on control plane (INFRA-872) overlapped with our repro runs.

Data to collect next time (commands to run as checklist):
- sudo cat /var/lib/kubelet/pki/ca.crt | sha256sum
- sudo stat -c '%a %U %G' /var/lib/kubelet/pki/*
- sudo systemctl show -p ExecStart kubelet
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager --since "10 minutes ago" | sed -n '1,200p'
- curl -v --cacert /var/lib/kubelet/pki/ca.crt https://<control-plane-ip>:6443/ - write out full TLS handshake debug

Notes for infra/AMI team:
- Suspect race/permissions in cloud-init -> kubelet startup ordering. Recommend adding an explicit gating script to AMI packer that ensures kubelet bootstrap artifacts are present and have correct ownership and SELinux labels before enabling service.
- If we change systemd PrivateTmp or other sandboxing flags we need to test cloud-init interactions explicitly.

Log snippets for ticket INFRA-872 (copy to Jira):
- "Failed to register node: error validating node: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" (kubelet journal)
- cloud-init output shows: "chmod: cannot access '/var/lib/kubelet/bootstrap-kubelet.conf': No such file or directory" then later "cp: cannot create regular file '/var/lib/kubelet/bootstrap-kubelet.conf': Permission denied"

Quick TODOs:
- [ ] Add kubelet ExecStartPre test in AMI
- [ ] Rebuild AMI without PrivateTmp drop-in and smoke test
- [ ] Reproduce with older kernel image
- [ ] Add ephemeral debug automation to autoscaler to avoid auto-terminate during repros
- [ ] Paste findings + logs into INFRA-872 and @eng-platform-engineering in Slack

Misc scratch ideas:
- Could bypass bootstrap complexity by baking node certs into AMI for a short-lived repro (not for production).
- Consider using cloud-init unit to systemctl mask kubelet until bootstrap conf exists then unmask+start.

If anyone picks this up, start with the cloud-init logs on a failed instance and the kubelet journal; both gave the strongest clues. - Jordan
